BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r7.claim: Accumulating wealth explains the mockery: self-admiration over money makes a person imagine wealth confers honor and superiority, so he belittles others; the phrase is appositional rather than a grammatical adjective of the indefinite ‘every.’
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r7.anchor: بدل من كل كأنه قيل ويل للذي جمع مالا وإنما وصفه الله بهذا الوصف المعنوي

BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r8.claim: He repeatedly counts and hoards wealth without discharging God’s due; an alternate reading with the doubled consonant separated supports the sense ‘counted it,’ while another reading makes it provisions for future calamities.
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r8.anchor: أي عده مرة بعد أخرى من غير أن يؤدي حق الله منه

BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r9.claim: The accumulation signals appetitive power and repeated counting signals ignorance: wealth itself attracts the calamities through which divine wisdom disperses it, so it cannot ward them off.
BURSEVI:v10p391#2/r9.anchor: لا يعلم أن نفس ذلك المال هو الذي يجر إليه النوائب

QASHANI:104:1-3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:104:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:104:1-3/r2.claim: Counting wealth reflects ignorance: its owner thinks it reserves against calamity, though divine wisdom disperses wealth through calamities.
QASHANI:104:1-3/r2.anchor: إشارة أيضا إلى الجهل لأن الذي جعل المال عدة للنوائب لا يعلم أن نفس ذلك المال يجر إليه النوائب

QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.claim: Ignorance, a vice of the royal faculty, is the root of all vices; the immersed deserve eternal punishment that overwhelms the heart and destroys its substance.
QASHANI:104:1-3/r4.anchor: والحاصل أن الجهل الذي هو رذيلة القوة الملكية أصل جميع الرذائل ومستلزم لها

QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r6.claim: The word for gathering is read with a doubled consonant to convey accumulation, or without doubling.

QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r14.claim: Those who rely on wealth, status, or their obedience are respectively poor, contemptible, and bankrupt.
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r14.anchor: ويقال : الفقير من استغنى بماله ، والحقير : من استغنى بجاهه ، والمفلس : من استغنى بطاعته

QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r15.claim: Relying on anything besides God makes one lowly; relying on God is true nobility.
QUSHAYRI:v3p447/r15.anchor: والذليل : من استغنى بغير الله ، والجليل : من استغنى بالله

SULAMI:v2p420/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p420/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p420/r1.claim: One rich in money is poor, one rich in status contemptible, one rich in obedience bankrupt, and one rich in kin lowly; only the one rich in his Lord is truly wealthy.
SULAMI:v2p420/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : من كان غناه بماله فهو فقير ، ومن كان غناه بجاهه فهو حقير

SULAMI:v2p420/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p420/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p420/r2.claim: Accumulating wealth signals ignorance, loving it signals hypocrisy, and hoarding it signals unbelief.
SULAMI:v2p420/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : جمع المال من علامة الجهل ، وحب المال من علامة النفاق

TUSTARI:104:2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:104:2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:104:2/r1.claim: The miser makes his wealth a servant to worldly life.

AKHFASH:v2p584/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p584/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p584/r1.claim: عدده derives from العدة, counting or enumerating his wealth.

FARRA:v3p289#2/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p289#2/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p289#2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar read جمع with gemination; ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ, and al-Ḥasan read it light.
FARRA:v3p289#2/r3.anchor: ثقل : جمع. الأعمش وأبو جعفر المدني

FARRA:v3p289#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p289#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p289#2/r4.claim: All read وعدده with gemination, meaning he counted and kept track of his wealth; al-Ḥasan's light reading was glossed by some as counting his clan.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the one who gathers and counts wealth as having enumerated it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3463#2/r1.anchor: عن السدى في قوله : جمع مالا وعدده قال : احصاه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r1.claim: The word māl can denote camels kept for blood money, orchards among agricultural communities, or cash among Meccans, a trading people; reports about the Anṣār, Abū Ṭalḥa, and al-ʿAbbās illustrate these senses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r1.anchor: وغلب عند أهل مكة على الدراهم لأن أهل مكة أهل تجر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r2.claim: Addadahu means he repeatedly counts it, with the doubled form intensifying his obsessive repetition and love of accumulating wealth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r3.claim: The majority read jamaʿa with an ungeminated mīm; the doubled addadahu then implies repeated counting, which indirectly suggests repeated accumulation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { جمع مالا } بتخفيف الميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r4.claim: These readers geminate the mīm in jamaʿa, intensifying accumulation in parallel with the doubled addadahu.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r4.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب وخلف بتشديد الميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r5.claim: Alternatively, addadahu can mean increasing the number or types of wealth, like the enumerated riches of 3:14.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p538/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { عدده } بمعنى أكثر إعداده

NAHHAS:v5p287/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p287/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p287/r6.claim: الذي may be nominative meaning he is the one, accusative as an explanatory I mean, or genitive as an apposition to كل.
NAHHAS:v5p287/r6.anchor: الذي في موضع رفع بمعنى هو الذي ويجوز النصب بمعنى أعني الذي ويجوز الخفض على البدل من كل

NAHHAS:v5p287/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p287/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
NAHHAS:v5p287/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Yahya ibn Wathab, al-Aʿmash, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read جمع with gemination.
NAHHAS:v5p287/r7.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي ( جمع ) بالتشديد

NAHHAS:v5p287/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p287/r8.speaker: الحسن وابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو وشيبة ونافع
NAHHAS:v5p287/r8.claim: Hasan, Ibn Kathir, Asim, Abu Amr, Shayba, and Nafiʿ read جمع without gemination; the light form can denote little or much, while the doubled form denotes much.
NAHHAS:v5p287/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو وشيبة ونافع ( جمع ) قال أبو جعفر جمع بالتخفيف

NAHHAS:v5p287/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p287/r9.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p287/r9.claim: Hasan has a noncanonical light reading of وعدده; if it means he counted it, the pronunciation makes the doubled consonant explicit, an option Nahhas says is remote except in poetry.
NAHHAS:v5p287/r9.anchor: وروي عن الحسن ( وعدده ) بالتخفيف وهي قراءة شاذة إن كان يريد عده ثم أظهر التضعيف

NAHHAS:v5p287/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p287/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p287/r10.claim: If وعدده means he gathered his wealth and counted its number, the word is a valid direct object.
NAHHAS:v5p287/r10.anchor: وإن كان يريد جمع مالا وجمع عدده على أنه مفعول أي أحصى عدده فهو جائز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r14.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي والحسن وأبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r14.claim: They read جَمَّع with a doubled م; the remaining readers use the light consonant.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي والحسن وأبو جعفر: «جمع» بشدة الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r15.claim: وعدده means counting and guarding wealth against loss, which kept it from generosity and charitable spending.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r15.anchor: وقوله وعدده معناه: أحصاه وحافظ على عدده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r16.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#2/r16.claim: Muqatil interprets the phrase as preparing and storing wealth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r1.claim: The reading being discussed lightens both d consonants; one explanation is that the phrase means collected wealth and a number of things, though the alternative is strained.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p521#3/r1.anchor: «وعدده» بتخفيف الدالين، فقيل المعنى جمع مالا وعددا من عشرة،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وروح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r1.claim: These readers pronounce “jamaʿa” with a doubled mīm; the remaining readers pronounce it without doubling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وروح جمع بالتشديد والباقون بالتخفيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وابن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r2.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan, and Ibn Yaʿmar read “ʿaddadahu” with an undoubled dāl; the majority double it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r2.anchor: وعدده قرأ الجمهور بتشديد الدال وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي والحسن وابن يعمر بتخفيفها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r3.claim: Al-Suddī interprets “counted it” as enumerating the amount of wealth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r4.claim: ʿIkrima interprets it as preparing wealth to suffice for many years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r4.anchor: والثاني أعده لما يكفيه في السنين قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the doubled reading means he counts it for ages, while the light reading can mean collecting wealth and supporters.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p228/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج من قرأ عدده بالتشديد فمعناه عدده للدهور ومن قرأ عدده بالتخفيف فمعناه جمع مالا وعددا

IBNKATHIR:104:2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:104:2/r1.speaker: السدي وابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:104:2/r1.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Jarīr say the person piles wealth together and counts its amount, as in 70:18, “he gathers and hoards.”
IBNKATHIR:104:2/r1.anchor: وأحصى عدده كقوله : { وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَى } [ المعارج : 18 ] قاله السدي

IBNKATHIR:104:2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:104:2/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:104:2/r2.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb says wealth occupies him all day, piling one amount onto another; at night he sleeps like a corpse.
IBNKATHIR:104:2/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب في قوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r10.claim: The phrase alladhi may be an appositive to kull or an accusative of censure.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r10.anchor: الذى } بدل من كل . أو نصب على الذم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r11.claim: One reading intensifies the verb jama'a, matching the repeated count in the expression.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r11.anchor: وقرىء : ( جمع ) بالتشديد ، وهو مطابق لعدده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r12.claim: One explanation of addadahu is that he made wealth a provision against the contingencies of time.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r12.anchor: وقيل : { * عدده } جعله عدة لحوادث الدهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r13.claim: A reading with wa means he collected wealth and counted or enumerated it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r13.anchor: وقرىء : ( وعدده ) أي : جمع المال وضبط عدده وأحصاه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r14.claim: Another explanation is that he amassed wealth and people who support him; a person of addad has many helpers and resources.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r14.anchor: أو جمع ماله وقومه الذين ينصرونه ، من قولك : فلان ذو عدد وعدد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r15.claim: Alternatively, malan wa-addadahu means he amassed wealth and counted it, with the form simplified as in the cited word.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r15.anchor: وقيل : { مالا وعدده } معناه : وعده على فك الإدغام ، نحو : ضننوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r20.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r20.claim: Al-Hasan challenged a wealthy visitor about thousands he neither used to ransom a base person nor gave to a generous one; the man saved it against hardship, and Hasan said he would leave it to an ungrateful heir and return it to an unforgiving Lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p801/r20.anchor: وعن الحسن : أنه عاد موسرا فقال : ما تقول في ألوف لم أفتد بها من لئيم ولا تفضلت على كريم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r10.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r10.claim: He reads جمع مالا وعدده as collecting wealth and counting it.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r11.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r11.claim: He says the person counted the kinds of wealth he owned.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r12.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r12.claim: He says the person accumulated wealth to ward off blame.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r12.anchor: لما يكفيه من الشين , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r13.claim: Another possibility is that he stored it for his children to inherit or boasted of its amount.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p335/r13.anchor: اتخذ ماله لمن يرثه من أولاده . ويحتمل خامسا : أنه فاخر بعدده وكثرته

MUQATIL:104:1-9/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r4.claim: The man gathered and prepared wealth to buy servants and livestock.
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r4.anchor: يقول: الذي استعد مالا ليشترى به الخدم والحيوان

MUQATIL:104:1-9/r14.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r14.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r14.claim: Muqātil links the condemnation to the description of the man in 74:11–12 and says he owned gardens in Mecca and Taif whose bounty continued in both winter and summer.
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r14.anchor: وكان له حديقتان، حديقة بمكة، وحديقة بالطائف، كان لا ينقطع خيره شتاء ولا صيفا

MUQATIL:104:1-9/r15.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r15.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r15.claim: He glosses the phrase about present sons as heads of households and says al-Walīd had seven sons.
MUQATIL:104:1-9/r15.anchor: يعني أرباب البيوت، وكان له سبعة بنين، قال: ومهدت له تمهيدا

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.claim: The narrative says the man swore he could distribute his wealth throughout Quraysh while alive without exhausting it, and challenged the threat of poverty.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r2.anchor: قسم مالى يمينا وشمالا على قريش ما دمت حيا ما فنى، فكيف تعدنى الفقر

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.claim: He is told that the One who gave him his wealth can take it away; this affects him, and he begins counting his possessions.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r3.anchor: إن الذي أعطاك، قادر على أن يأخذه منك، فوقع في قلبه من ذلك شىء، ثم عمد إلى ماله فعده

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r4.claim: He counts and inventories his gold, silver, land, gardens, and slaves.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r4.anchor: ما كان ذهب أو فضة، أو أرض، أو حديقة، أو رقيق، فعده وأحصاه

MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.claim: He tells Muhammad that even if all his counted wealth were bread it would not run out, and the condemnation in Sūrat al-Humazah is revealed in response.
MUQATIL:104:1-5/r5.anchor: يا محمد تعدنى الفقر والله لو كان هذا خبزا ما فنى، فأنزل الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r1.claim: الذي is either an appositive to كل or an accusative of censure.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ الذي ﴾ بدل من كل أو نصب على الذم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r2.speaker: شامي
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r2.claim: The Syrian, Ḥamza, and ʿAlī reading doubles the verb جمع to emphasize amassing, matching وعدده.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ جمع مالا ﴾ جمع شامى وحمزة وعلى مبالغة جمع وهو مطابق لقوله ﴿ وعدده ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r3.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r3.claim: Ḥamza shares the intensified reading جمع.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r3.anchor: جمع شامى وحمزة وعلى مبالغة جمع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r4.speaker: على
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī shares the intensified reading جمع.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r4.anchor: جمع شامى وحمزة وعلى مبالغة جمع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r5.claim: He amassed the wealth and stored it as provision for disasters of the age.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p356#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ وعدده ﴾ أى جعله عدة لحوادث الدهر

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r1.claim: One view says he stores wealth against the adversities of time.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r2.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says he counts the amount of his wealth.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says he reserves wealth for his children to inherit.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: أي أعد ماله لمن يرثه من أولاده.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r4.claim: Another view says he boasts of the size and number of his holdings.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r5.claim: The point condemns hoarding wealth away from obedience, as in 68:12 and 70:18.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r5.anchor: والمقصود الذم على إمساك المال عن سبيل الطاعة

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r6.claim: Most readers lighten the mīm in jamʿ; Ibn ʿAmir, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi geminate it for abundance, which Abu ʿUbayd prefers because of “counted it.”
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r6.anchor: وقراءة الجماعة «جمع» مخفف الميم. وشددها ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي على التكثير.

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r7.speaker: الحسن ونصر بن عاصم وأبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, Nasr ibn ʿAsim, and Abu al-ʿAliyah lighten both words, voicing the doubled consonant; the author calls this unlikely given the two dal letters in writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r7.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ونصر بن عاصم وأبو العالية «جمع» مخففا، «وعدده» مخففا أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r8.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r8.claim: Al-Mahdawi says the light reading of ʿaddadahu coordinates with wealth as “counted his number,” not a verb used only poetically.
QURTUBI-FULL:104:2/r8.anchor: قال المهدوي: من خفف «وعدده» فهو معطوف على المال

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r1.claim: Quṭb identifies Sūrat al-Humaza as Meccan, with nine verses.

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r2.claim: The sura portrays a real pattern from the early mission that recurs everywhere: a mean, small-souled person lets wealth dominate and treats it as life’s highest value, believing it buys people’s dignity and honor.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r2.anchor: تعكس هذه السورة صورة من الصور الواقعية في حياة الدعوة في عهدها الأول . وهي في الوقت ذاته نموذج يتكرر في كل بيئة

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r3.claim: The wealthy person imagines money can do anything, including warding off death, securing lasting life, and escaping God’s decree and judgment.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r3.anchor: كما يروح يحسب أن هذا المال إله قادر على كل شيء ؛ لا يعجز عن فعل شيء ! حتى دفع الموت وتخليد الحياة

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r4.claim: He obsessively counts and enjoys counting wealth, then grows arrogant and belittles people through verbal mockery, gestures, and contempt for their traits.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r4.anchor: ينطلق في هوس بهذا المال يعده ويستلذ تعداده ؛ وتنطلق في كيانه نفخة فاجرة ، تدفعه إلى الاستهانة بأقدار الناس

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r5.claim: Islam abhors this faithless, ignoble character and forbids mockery and faultfinding elsewhere; Quṭb infers a real case of some polytheists targeting the Messenger and believers, but says reports naming individuals are unreliable.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r5.anchor: وقد وردت روايات بتعيين بعض الشخصيات . ولكنها ليست وثيقة . فنكتفي نحن بما قررناه عنها

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r6.claim: The warning pairs the mocker’s offense with fitting punishment: the arrogant money-backed scoffer is discarded into the crushing Fire, whose divine attribution marks it as uniquely terrifying.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r6.anchor: المهمل المتردي في( الحطمة )التي تحطم كل ما يلقى إليها

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r7.claim: The Fire reaches the heart that bred mockery and arrogance; it encloses the victim without rescue or concern, binding him to a pillar like an unrespected beast.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r7.anchor: هذه النار مغلقة عليه ، لا ينقذه منها أحد ، ولا يسأل عنه فيها أحد ! وهو موثق فيها إلى عمود كما توثق البهائم

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r8.claim: Harsh sound patterns and emphatic rhetorical devices intensify the threat: summary and obscurity, an awe-inspiring question, then explanation and amplification; the imagery and feeling match the mocker’s deed.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r8.anchor: وفي جرس الألفاظ تشديد : عدده . كلا . لينبذن . تطلع . ممددة وفي معاني العبارات توكيد بشتى أساليب التوكيد

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r9.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r9.claim: The Qur’an both follows and directs the mission; it is a decisive weapon that destroys opponents’ schemes, shakes enemies, and strengthens believers.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r9.anchor: لقد كان القرآن يتابع أحداث الدعوة ويقودها في الوقت ذاته . وكان هو السلاح البتار الصاعق

QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r10.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r10.claim: God’s response to the mocker condemns moral degradation and defends believers, assuring them God sees their humiliation, abhors it, and punishes it, thereby lifting their spirits above hostile schemes.
QUTB-ZILAL:104:2/r10.anchor: وإنا لنرى في عناية الله سبحانه بالرد على هذه الصورة معنيين كبيرين

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r1.claim: Al-ladhī is either an appositive to kull or an accusative expression of censure.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r1.anchor: { الذى } بدل من كل أو نصب على ذم

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r2.claim: The verse identifies wealth as the cause of mockery: its owner admires what he gathered, assumes it gives him superiority, and belittles others.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r2.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله تعالى بهذا الوصف لأنه يجري مجرى السبب والعلة في الهمز واللمز وهو إعجابه بما جمع من المال ، وظنه أن الفضل فيه لأجل ذلك فيستنقص غيره

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r3.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r3.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn ʿĀmir read jammaʿa with doubling; the others read jamaʿa lightly, with closely related meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وابن عامر جمع بالتشديد والباقون بالتخفيف والمعنى في جمع وجمع واحد متقارب

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r4.claim: The doubled reading suggests collecting wealth from here and there over an extended period, unlike the light reading.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r4.anchor: والفرق أن { جمع } بالتشديد يفيد أنه جمعه من ههنا وههنا ، وأنه لم يجمعه في يوم واحد ، ولا في يومين ، ولا في شهر ولا في شهرين

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r5.claim: The indefinite mālan may refer to the world's wealth collectively, making any individual's share too small to boast about.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r5.anchor: أحدهما : أن يقال : المال اسم لكل ما في الدنيا كما قال : { المال والبنون زينة الحيواة الدنيا } فمال الإنسان الواحد بالنسبة إلى مال كل الدنيا حقير

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite form magnifies the wealth as reaching the utmost in filth and corruption, making pride in it irrational.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r6.anchor: والثاني : أن يكون المراد منه التعظيم أي مال بلغ في الخبث والفساد أقصى النهايات . فكيف يليق بالعاقل أن يفتخر به

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r7.claim: One reading of ʿaddadahu derives it from ʿudda, stored provision: he keeps wealth as a reserve against the age's calamities.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r7.anchor: أحدها أنه مأخوذ من العدة وهي الذخيرة يقال : أعددت الشيء لكذا وعددته إذا أمسكته له وجعلته عدة وذخيرة لحوادث الدهر

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r8.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī takes ʿaddadahu as counting wealth; the repeated form conveys much counting, as he says item by item that each thing is his, and is distracted by wealth by day and hides it at night.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r8.anchor: ولهذا قال السدي : وعدده أي أحصاه يقول : هذا لي وهذا لي يلهيه ماله بالنهار فإذا جاء الليل كان يخفيه

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r9.claim: A third meaning is that he multiplied the wealth, as in describing a clan as having great numbers.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r9.anchor: وثالثها : عدده أي كثره يقال : في بني فلان عدد أي كثرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r10.claim: Some read ʿaddadahu without doubling: either he gathered, controlled, and counted his wealth, or he counted his numerous supporters, increasing his grounds for boasting.
RAZI-FULL:v32p87#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم وعدده بالتخفيف وفيه وجهان أحدهما : أن يكون المعنى جمع المال وضبط عدده وأحصاه وثانيهما : جمع ماله وعدد قومه الذين ينصرونه من قولك فلان ذو عدد وعدد إذا كان له عدد وافر من الأنصار

STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah focuses on the torment awaiting people who spend worldly life hoarding wealth.
STUDYQURAN:104:intro/r6.anchor: focus upon the torment that awaits one who spends the life of this world hoarding wealth

STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.claim: The hoarder's punishment is vividly described in 9:34–35: hoarded gold and silver brand their owners in Hell.
STUDYQURAN:104:2/r1.anchor: The punishment for those who hoard is most vividly described in 9:34–35

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r1.claim: الذي جمع may be genitive as an appositive, or accusative or nominative by disjunction; it cannot be a genitive adjective or explanatory apposition because its definiteness differs.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r1.anchor: يجوز جره بدلا، ونصبه ورفعه على القطع. ولا يجوز جره نعتا ولا بيانا لتغايرهما تعريفا وتنكيرا

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r2.speaker: الأخوان وابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r2.claim: Al-Akhawān and Ibn ʿĀmir read جمع with a doubled mīm for intensification and to match عدده.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r2.anchor: وقوله: " جمع " قرأ الأخوان وابن عامر بتشديد الميم على المبالغة والتكثير، ولأنه يوافق " عدده "

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r3.claim: The remaining readers pronounce جمع with a light mīm, a form that can imply either intensive or non-intensive gathering.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r3.anchor: والباقون " جمع " مخففا وهي محتملة للتكثير وعدمه

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r4.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r4.claim: The common reading doubles the first dāl of وعدده, also conveying intensification.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r4.anchor: العامة على تثقيل الدال الأول، وهو أيضا للمبالغة

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r5.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī read the first dāl of وعدده lightly.

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r6.claim: One interpretation is that he gathered wealth and counted it, with عدده functioning as a noun for its tally, meaning he enumerated it.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r6.anchor: أن المعنى: جمع مالا وعدد ذلك المال، أي: وجمع عدده، أي: أحصاه

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r7.claim: A second interpretation takes عدده as the number of the man’s clan and relatives, whom he gathered around himself.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r7.anchor: الثاني: أن المعنى: وجمع عدد نفسه من عشيرته وأقاربه، و " عدده " على هذين التأويلين اسم معطوف على " مالا "

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r8.claim: A third analysis reads عدده as a past verb meaning عده, though that form is irregular in its expression.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r8.anchor: الثالث: أن " عدده " فعل ماض بمعنى عده، إلا أنه شذ في إظهاره كما شذ في قوله

SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r9.claim: The irregular verbal form is illustrated by an unattributed poetic line beginning إني أجود لأقوام وإن ضننوا.
SAMIN-DURR:104:2/r9.anchor:
كما شذ في قوله:
4641...................
إني أجود لأقوام وإن ضننوا

TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r1.claim: The verse describes someone who gathered and counted wealth, hoarded it, withheld spending in God’s way, and failed to pay God’s due from it.
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r1.anchor: وقد ذكر عن بعض المتقدمين بإسناد غير ثابت، أنه قرأه: «جمع مالا وعدده»

TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that Abū Jaʿfar and most Kūfans except ʿĀṣim use doubled mīm, while the Medina/Ḥijāz and Basran readers except Abū Jaʿfar, along with ʿĀṣim, use light mīm; the meanings are close.
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r2.anchor: والحجاز، سوى أبي جعفر وعامة قراء البصرة، ومن الكوفة عاصم، {جمع} [الهمزة: 2] بالتخفيف،

TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r3.speaker: قراء الأمصار
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r3.claim: All regional readers agree on doubling the dāl in ʿaddadahu, in the sense of counting the wealth.
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r3.anchor: وكلهم مجمعون على تشديد الدال من {عدده} [الهمزة: 2] على الوجه الذي ذكرت من تأويله.

TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects an unreliably transmitted early reading with a light dāl, which would mean he gathered and counted his clan, because it opposes the accepted regional reading.
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r4.anchor: تخفيف الدال، بمعنى: جمع مالا، وجمع عشيرته وعدده. هذه قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها

TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts either doubled or light mīm in jamaʿa because both are established regional readings with close meanings.
TAB-FULL:v24p620#2/r5.anchor: وأما قوله: {جمع مالا} [الهمزة: 2] فإن التشديد والتخفيف فيهما صوابان، لأنهما قراءتان معروفتان في قرأة الأمصار، متقاربتا المعنى

ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r6.claim: The verb for collecting wealth is reported with a light and a doubled consonant reading.
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r6.anchor: وقرئت: (الذي جمع مالا)، وقرئت (جمع مالا)، بالتخفيف

ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r7.claim: The verb ʿaddadahu is read with the consonant doubled or lightened.

ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r8.claim: With the doubled reading, he counted or kept counting the wealth over long stretches of time.

ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r9.claim: With the light reading, he collected wealth and numbers, meaning a group of people he prepared as supporters.
ZAJJAJ:v5p361/r9.anchor: ومن قرأ (وعدده) فمعناه جمع مالا وعددا، أي وقوما أعدهم نصارا

TABATABAI:104:1-3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r6.claim: The hoarding and counting describe the slanderer; the indefinite money belittles it, since wealth only meets immediate bodily needs such as food and water.
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r6.anchor: للتحقير فإن المال وإن كثر ما كثر لا يغني عن صاحبه شيئا غير أن له منه ما يصرفه في حوائج

TABATABAI:104:1-3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r7.claim: Addadahu derives from counting: attachment to wealth makes the person amass it and count it again and again for pleasure; an alternative says he stores it for future hardship.
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r7.anchor: من العد بمعنى الإحصاء أي إنه لحبه المال وشغفه بجمعه يجمع المال ويعده عدا بعد عد التذاذا بتكثره. وقيل المعنى

TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.claim: Attachment to earth and endless hope make him crave more than life's brief needs; he mistakes wealth for immortality, and the accumulation and perceived self-sufficiency produce tyranny and superiority over others.
TABATABAI:104:1-3/r9.anchor: زاد مالا زاد حرصا إلى ما لا نهاية له فظاهر حاله أنه يرى أن المال يخلده، ولحبه الغريزي للبقاء يهتم

TABRISI:104:1-9/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9/r1.speaker: أهل البصرة، ابن كثير، نافع، عاصم
TABRISI:104:1-9/r1.claim: Basran readers, Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and ʿĀṣim read “gathered” with a light consonant; other readers geminate it.
TABRISI:104:1-9/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل البصرة وابن كثير ونافع وعاصم جمع بالتخفيف

TABRISI:104:1-9/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:104:1-9/r3.claim: Abū al-Hasan says the geminated reading is more usual because a person gathers money from different places.
TABRISI:104:1-9/r3.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: المثقلة أكثر تقول فلان يجمع المال

TABRISI:104:1-9/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:104:1-9/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr says the light form can mean gathering many things, while the geminated form suggests gathering one item after another.
TABRISI:104:1-9/r4.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: وجمع خفيفة إذا أكثر وإذا ثقل فإنما هو شيء بعد شيء

TABRISI:104:1-9/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9/r5.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:104:1-9/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows the light form for gathering something within a short period rather than successively; an example speaks of assembling everyone.
TABRISI:104:1-9/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: وقد يجوزأن يكون جمع لما يجمع فيما قرب

TABRISI:104:1-9/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:104:1-9/r6.claim: War equipment is unlikely to be gathered all at once, so successive gathering is plausible under either reading.
TABRISI:104:1-9/r6.anchor: والأشبه أن تكون أداة الحرب لا تجمع في وقت واحد وإنما هو شيء بعد شيء

TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r3.claim: “The one who amassed” is parsed as a genitive apposition to hamza, or as a supplied explanation in accusative or a subject in nominative; a codex variant makes it adjectival.
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r3.anchor: الذي جمع في موضع جر على البدل من همزة ولا يجوز أن يكون صفة

TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the hoarder counted and tallied his money.

TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r11.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r11.claim: Al-Zajjāj says he counted money for future ages, treating the verb as making provision and retaining something in reserve.
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r11.anchor: عدده للدهور فيكون من العدة عن الزجاج

TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r12.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r12.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the person collected money unlawfully, withheld its due, and stored it for future calamities.
TABRISI:104:1-9#2/r12.anchor: جمع مالا من غير حله ومنعه من حقه وأعده ذخرا

THALABI:v10p286/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r4.speaker: شيبة ونافع وعاصم وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأيوب
THALABI:v10p286/r4.claim: These readers lighten the mīm in جَمَعَ; Abū Ḥātim chooses this reading.
THALABI:v10p286/r4.anchor: قرأ شيبة ونافع وعاصم وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأيوب بتخفيف الميم، واختاره أبو حاتم

THALABI:v10p286/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r5.speaker: غيرهم وأبو عبيد
THALABI:v10p286/r5.claim: Other readers geminate the mīm in جَمَّعَ; Abū ʿUbayd chooses this reading, while Yaʿqūb's reading is disputed.
THALABI:v10p286/r5.anchor: غيرهم بالتشديد واختاره أبو عبيد، واختلف فيه عن يعقوب

THALABI:v10p286/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p286/r6.claim: The author glosses وعَدَّدَه as having counted the wealth.

THALABI:v10p286/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r7.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p286/r7.claim: Muqātil says the person prepared and stored the wealth, making it provisions for himself.
THALABI:v10p286/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل: استعده وذخره وجعله عتادا له

THALABI:v10p286/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r8.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p286/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads وعَدَّدَه with a light dāl; the author considers this reading remote.
THALABI:v10p286/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعدده بالتخفيف وهو بعيد

THALABI:v10p286/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p286/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p286/r9.claim: The author notes that poetry can similarly lighten a doubled consonant, citing an anonymous poet as evidence.
THALABI:v10p286/r9.anchor: وقد جاء مثل ذلك في الشعر لما أبرزوا التضعيف خففوه، قال الشاعر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r1.claim: The verse is read both with doubled and light dāl in jamaʿa; Abū al-Ḥasan says the doubled reading is more common in speech, describing accumulation from place to place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r1.anchor: وقرئ "جمع" بالتشديد (¬3)، قال أبو الحسن (¬4): المثقلة أكثر في الكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr says the light reading means having amassed much; the doubled form emphasizes gathering item after item.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: "جمع" بالتخفيف إذا كثر، ومن ثقل فإنما هو شيء بعد شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r3.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r3.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the light form can also mean collecting things one by one, which fits how people ordinarily gather stores over time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع بالتخفيف لما يجمع شيء بعد شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r4.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r4.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line about a man collecting equipment for difficult times is cited as evidence that the light reading can convey gradual accumulation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p308/r4.anchor:
الأعشى) (¬5):
لامرئ يجمع الأداة ... لريب الدهر لا مسند ولا زمال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses ʿaddadahu as counting or tallying the wealth.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says he kept the wealth for a long time; Muqātil similarly says he prepared or stored wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r2.anchor: الزجاج: "وعدده" للدهر (¬6)، وهو معنى قول مقاتل: واستعد # مالا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r3.claim: The author of al-Naẓm derives the word from ʿuddah, provision or reserve, and says it can mean keeping something ready for a purpose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r3.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: مأخوذ من العدة، وهو الذخيرة، يقال: أعدد الشيء لكذا وأعددته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r4.claim: Another gloss is that he made his wealth numerous; ʿadad and ʿadīd can describe a large quantity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p309/r4.anchor: صاحب النظم) (¬5): وقيل معنى "وعدده" كثره، كما يقال: هذا مال له عدد

WAHIDI-QT:104:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:104:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:104:2/r1.claim: The miser has prepared his wealth for the future; another interpretation is that he accumulated a great quantity.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:104:1-4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:104:1-4/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:104:1-4/r2.claim: He amassed and prepared wealth for the future; alternatively, he counted it repeatedly in great quantity.

ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.claim: The surah condemns slander and fault-finding alongside amassing wealth and treating it as protection that will secure immortality.
ASAD-NOTES:104:1/r1.anchor: WOE unto every slanderer, fault-finder! [1] (104:2) [Woe unto him[2]] who amasses wealth and counts it a safeguard

ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.claim: Asad inserts the repeated “Woe unto him” because verses 2–3 describe a blameworthy attitude distinct from the two types in verse 1.
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n2/r1.anchor: This repetitive interpolation is necessary because the blameworthy attitude spoken of in verses 2-3 obviously belongs to a category entirely different

ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r2.claim: Asad bases his rendering of addadahu as “counts it a safeguard” on Jawhari's lexical explanation.
ASAD-NOTES:104:1#n3/r2.anchor: My rendering of 'addadahu in the preceding verse as "[he] counts it a safeguard" is based on Jawhari's explanation

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.claim: Woe formulas followed by vice catalogues also occur at 107:4–7, 83:1–3, 83:10–11, 52:11–12, and 51:60; 83:1–6 is especially close in its wealth theme and following rhetorical question.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Durch wail eingeleitete Wehsprüche mit folgendem Lasterkatalog finden sich sonst noch in 107:4–7, 83:1–3, 83:10.11 und 52:11.12

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.claim: Woe speeches as a basic form of prophetic discourse already appear in the Hebrew Bible, for example Micah 2:1–3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-3:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Wehsprüche als grundlegende Form prophetischer Rede begegnen bereits in der Hebräischen Bibel

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:2:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:2:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:2:anmerkung/r1.claim: The perfect in “gathered wealth and counted it” is aspectual, which motivates translating it with the German present tense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:2:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Da es sich um ein aspektuelles Perfekt handeln dürfte (vgl. die Anmerkung zu 96:1.2), wurde mit dem deutschen Präsens übersetzt.

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.claim: The opening woe, vice list, and insult sketch a prototypical sinner who trusts without basis that money grants immortality, driving antisocial conduct and limitless accumulation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r1.anchor: Der einleitende Wehspruch mit Lasterkatalog (V. 1.2) sowie das anschließende Scheltwort entwerfen das Charakterporträt eines prototypischen Sünders.

CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.claim: This hoarding is the opposite of ostentatious spending criticized at 90:6, yet both reflect the delusion that people can secure immortality by their own power.
CORPUSCORANICUM:104:1-4:kommentar/r2.anchor: Das kritisierte Verhalten bildet damit das genaue Gegenteil der in 90:6 angeprangerten ostentativen Besitzverschwendung

ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r9.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, Kisai, Abu Jaʿfar, Rawh, Khalaf, and Aʿmash read jamʿa with a doubled mīm in the intensive form, emphasizing accumulation.
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r9.anchor: İbn Âmir, Hamza, Kisâî, Ebû Cafer, Revh, Halef ve A‘meş, mîm’in teşdîdiyle tef‘îl bâbından جَمَعَ okumuşlardır

ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r10.claim: The person accumulates wealth from everywhere, then keeps counting and increasing it.

ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r11.claim: He counts without considering the wealth's sources, obligations, or possible good uses, or he boasts of it before a circle of flatterers and gathers them around himself.
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r11.anchor: nereden gelip nereye gitmesi lâzım geleceğini, onunla ne gibi hayırlar yapabileceğini düşünmeyerek

ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r12.claim: Many in the humaza lumaza circle own little themselves but aspire to collect wealth through slander, so they cluster around and count the rich person's wealth.
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r12.anchor: Yahut etrafındakilere sade onu saydırıp onunla iftihar etmek

ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r13.claim: The relative is singular because it can describe each individual, while the later plural pronoun points to the gathered group.
ELMALILI:104:1-9#3/r13.anchor: Sonra da bunların cem‘iyyetine tenbih için عَلَيْهِم diye cemi‘zamiri gönderilmiştir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r1.claim: Sūrah al-Humazah counters al-ʿAṣr: instead of urging truth and steadfastness, the miserly hoard wealth and taunt people who urge others to fulfill God's and fellow people's rights, hoping to demoralize them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r1.anchor: reveals a clear similarity in their themes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r2.claim: Miserliness and wealth hoarding recur elsewhere in the Qur'an; 9:79 condemns those who censure believers' generous giving and mock poor givers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r3.claim: Mutatawwi and mutatawwa describe someone who fulfills obligations and eagerly performs optional acts beyond them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r3.anchor: only fulfils his obligations but also enjoys doing what is optional

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r5.claim: The cited verse describes hypocrites who neither give in God's cause nor tolerate seeing others give.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p445/r5.anchor: the hypocrites do not spend in the cause of God and also cannot bear to see others doing so

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r3.claim: The stingy mockers silence those urging them to fulfill God’s and fellow humans’ rights while amassing and hoarding wealth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r3.anchor: they try to silence those who call upon them to fulfil the rights of God and their own fellow beings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r4.claim: Calculating wealth occupies their minds, including business prospects, investment gains, offsetting losses, and next year’s total.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r4.anchor: deeply engrossed in computing and calculating their wealth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r5.claim: They ridicule someone who gives to orphans and the poor as showing off, while claiming their own thousands in spending go unnoticed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p448/r5.anchor: they make fun of him by saying that he is only

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r1.claim: These readers read جمع lightly; the remaining readers geminate it as جمّع, with the latter described as more common in recitation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم: جمع خفيفا، وقرأ الباقون: جمع* بالتشديد .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r2.claim: Abu Amr distinguishes light جمع for a large accumulation from geminated جمّع for collecting item by item; Abu al-Hasan agrees that the geminated form fits this verse.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r2.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: المثقلة أكثر في القراءة، تقول: يجمع الأموال، أي: يجمعها من هنا ومن هنا، قال: وقال أبو عمرو:

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r3.claim: The light reading can also describe gradual collection if it happens over a short period; poetry about gathering tools and ants shows accumulation may still occur item by item.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p441/r3.anchor: وقال : ولها بالماطرون إذا أكل النمل الذي جمعا والنمل لا يجمع ما يدخر في وقت واحد

QIRAAT-ER:104:2:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:104:2:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:104:2:2#1/r1.claim: Form II jammaʿa intensifies gathering, suggesting persistent or excessive accumulation rather than a single act; both Forms I and II are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:104:2:2#1/r1.anchor: Form II intensive jamma'a (gemination of middle radical) — intensifies the gathering

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r9.claim: الذي is either appositional or accusative as a condemnation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r9.anchor: الذي: بدل، أو نصب على الذم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r10.speaker: الحسن، أبو جعفر، ابن عامر، الأخوان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r10.claim: They read جمع with a doubled mīm; the other canonical readers read it without doubling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p540/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والأخوان: جمع مشدد الميم وباقي السبعة: بالتخفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r1.claim: ‘The one who gathered wealth’ may be an appositive to kull, a partitive appositive, or—according to al-Jarbardī—an adjective because kull is definite; Alusi questions that last analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r1.anchor: ( الذي جمع مالا ) بدل من كل بدل وقيل بدل بعض من كل وقال الجار بردى يجوز أن يكون صفة له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r2.claim: The phrase may instead be accusative or nominative as a construction of dispraise.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا أو مرفوعا على الذم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r3.claim: The indefinite ‘wealth’ can magnify its quantity; those who say the sura was revealed about al-Akhnas report four thousand dinars, or ten thousand.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r3.anchor: وتنكير ملا للتفخيم والتكثير وقد كان عند القائلين انها نزلت في لاخنس أربعة لآلاف دينار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r4.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite can belittle the wealth as insignificant and contemptible before God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للتحقير والتقليل باعتبار أنه عند الله تعالى أقل وأحقر شىء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r5.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والاخوان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, and the two Ḥamzas read جمع with a doubled mīm, conveying repeated accumulation and fitting ‘he counted it repeatedly.’
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والاخوان جمع بشد الميم للتكثير

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r6.claim: The mainstream وعدده means that he counted the wealth repeatedly, out of love and intense attachment to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r6.anchor: أي عده مرة بعد أخرى حباله وشغفا به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r7.claim: Another view says he made the wealth into different classes and kinds, such as real estate and coins; this is cited in al-Taʾwīlāt.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r7.anchor: وقيل جعله أصنافا وأنواعا كعقار ونقوده حكاه في التاويلات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r8.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r8.claim: Several commentators say he made the wealth a reserve stored for the calamities of time.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r8.anchor: وقال غير واحد أى جعله عة ومدخرا لنوائب الدهر ومصائبه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r9.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī read وعدده with a light mīm, which can be a past-tense verb meaning ‘he counted it,’ with de-gemination contrary to regular analogy, as in the cited line.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والكلبي وعدده بالتخفيف فقيل معناه وعده فهو فعل ماضي فك ادغامه على خلاف القيلس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r10.claim: The cited poetic line supplies a comparison for the lightened verb’s unusual de-gemination.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r10.anchor: كما في قوله مهلا اعاذل هل جربت من خلقي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r11.claim: The lightened form may instead be the noun ‘number,’ coordinated with wealth: he gathered wealth, tallied its amount, and recorded it; counting already entails enumeration, so no strained ellipsis is needed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r11.anchor: وقيل هو اسم بمعنى العدد المعروف معطوف على ماله أي جمع ماله وضبط عدده وأحصاه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r12.claim: Alusi says both explanations of the lightened reading support the first interpretation of the mainstream reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r12.anchor: وعلى الوجهين ايد بالقراءة المذكورة المعنى الاول لقراءة الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r13.claim: A further view takes ʿadad as followers and supporters; coordinated with wealth, it means he gathered his assets and the people who defend him.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p230/r13.anchor: وقيل هو اسم بمعنى الاتباع والانصار يقال فلان ذو عدد وعدد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r1.claim: Abu Jafar, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai read jamʿa with a doubled mīm to convey intensive accumulation; the others read it without doubling.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر، وابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي: "جمع" بتشديد الميم على التكثير،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r2.claim: ʿAddadahu means he counted it; Muqatil says he prepared and stored it as provision, since the verb can mean keeping something back.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p530/r2.anchor: {وعدده} أحصاه، وقال مقاتل: استعده وادخره وجعله عتادا له،

BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r4.claim: The description can grammatically substitute for every slanderer or be a censure in the accusative or nominative; Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read with a doubled mīm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r4.anchor: بدل من كل أو ذم منصوب أو مرفوع، وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بالتشديد

BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r5.claim: He made wealth provision for calamities or accumulated it repeatedly; a variant separates the doubling.
BAYDAWI-FULL:104:1-3/r5.anchor: وجعله عدة للنوازل أو عدة مرة بعد أخرى

BINTSHATI:v2p170/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read jammaʿa with doubled mīm; the other readers use the undoubled form.

BINTSHATI:v2p170/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r3.claim: Readers agree on doubled dāl in ʿaddadahu apart from an unsupported light reading; al-Ṭabarī rejects that reading for opposing the regional consensus.
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r3.anchor: وهذه قراءة لا أستجيز القراءة بها، لخلافها قراءة الأمصار

BINTSHATI:v2p170/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī interprets the public reading as collecting, preserving, and counting wealth without spending for God's cause or paying its due.
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r4.anchor: جمع مالاً وحفظه وأحصى عدده ولم ينفقه في سبيل الله

BINTSHATI:v2p170/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r5.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī says the doubled reading suggests accumulating wealth from many places over time, unlike the undoubled form.
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r5.anchor: إن جمع بالتشديد يفيد أنه جمعه من ههنا وههنا

BINTSHATI:v2p170/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r6.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī offers storage as provision for calamities, counting, tallying, or a large retinue as meanings of ʿaddadahu.
BINTSHATI:v2p170/r6.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من العدة وهي الذخيرة لحوادث الدهر

BINTSHATI:v2p171/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r1.claim: Jamʿ means bringing together scattered, varied individuals and names a group, mixed people, a gathering, or the act of assembling.
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r1.anchor: والجمع في اللغة ضد التفرق، مع ملحظ من التفاوت بين أفراده

BINTSHATI:v2p171/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r2.claim: Religious usages include congregational prayer and the Day of Gathering, when varied peoples, classes, and beliefs assemble.
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r2.anchor: كما سمى اليوم الآخر يوم الجمع، يجمع الناس على اختلاف أجناسهم

BINTSHATI:v2p171/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r3.claim: The simple verb occurs eighteen times with its root sense of gathering scattered things; the doubled form has no Qur'anic derivative.
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r3.anchor: وجاء الفعل ثلاثياً ثماني عشرة مرة

BINTSHATI:v2p171/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r4.claim: In thirteen instances God gathers people in guidance, reassembles bones, or gathers humanity for Judgment and the Day of Decision.
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r4.anchor: منها ثلاث عشرة مرة، الفعل فيها مسند إلى الله سبحانه

BINTSHATI:v2p171/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r5.claim: Other examples include possessions people gather and the massing of troops and weapons against believers.
BINTSHATI:v2p171/r5.anchor: الذين قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم

BINTSHATI:v2p172/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r1.claim: The prohibition on joining two sisters is an exception to separation of bloodlines; the survey shows jamʿ evokes massing and mingling.
BINTSHATI:v2p172/r1.anchor: ولا يتختلف الملحظ في آية المحارم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the warning to 103:2: the collector imagines himself complete and faults others, while relying on wealth to preserve him; these are signs of human deficiency.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r3.anchor: رإن الإنسان لفي خسر } أتبعه بمثال من ذكر نقصه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r4.claim: The description singles out a wealthy person who needs no hoarding yet collects money, because people regard profit as success and boast of it; collecting wealth is the first sign of his loss.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r4.anchor: وكان المتمول عندهم هو الرابح , وهم يتفاخرون بالربح

BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read jamʿa with doubling, intensifying abundant collection; other reciters use the lighter form, while all double ʿaddada because the bare form can denote little.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p525/r5.anchor: جاء التشديد في فعله لأبي جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r1.claim: The collected wealth is substantial; he counts it until enumeration would take a long time, or stores and hoards it for future worldly needs.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p526/r1.anchor: أي جعله بحيث إذا أريد عدده طال الزمان فيه وكثر التعداد

DURR:104:2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:104:2/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR:104:2/r1.claim: Al-Suddī explains ‘he gathered wealth and counted it’ to mean that he counted or reckoned it; Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits the report.
DURR:104:2/r1.anchor: عن السدي في قوله : { جمع مالاً وعدده } قال : أحصاه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r1.claim: The doubled reading of ʿaddadahu means he counted and kept track of his wealth; another explanation makes it provision against future calamities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r1.anchor: وعدده بشد الدال الأولى: أي أحصاه وحافظ عليه. وقيل: جعله عدة لطوارق الدهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r2.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī lighten both consonants, meaning he gathered money and carefully counted it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r2.anchor: والحسن والكلبي: بتخفيفهما، أي جمع المال وضبط عدده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r3.claim: Another reading or interpretation makes the object his numerous clansmen; an unassimilated form is supported by a poetic line.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r3.anchor: وقيل: وعددا من عشيرته. وقيل: وعدده على ترك الإدغام، كقوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r6.claim: Reports give al-Akhnas's fortune as either four thousand or ten thousand dinars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p541/r6.anchor: قيل: وكان للأخنس أربعة آلاف دينار. وقيل: عشرة آلاف دينار

ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r1.claim: الَّذِي is either an appositive or accusative by way of censure.
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r1.anchor: { الذي } : بدل ، أو نصب على الذم

ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r2.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والأخوان
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿAmir, and the two Hamza and Kisai read جَمَّعَ with a doubled m; the rest of the seven read it lightly.
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والأخوان : جمع مشدد الميم ؛ وباقي السبعة : بالتخفيف

ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r3.claim: The majority double the first dāl in عَدَّدَهُ, meaning that he counted and carefully kept the money.
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r3.anchor: والجمهور : { وعدده } بشد الدال الأولى : أي أحصاه وحافظ عليه

ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that he kept the money as a reserve against the vicissitudes of time.

ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r5.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi read both verbs lightly: he collected money and accurately counted it.
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r5.anchor: والحسن والكلبي : بتخفيفهما ، أي جمع المال وضبط عدده

ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r6.claim: A further interpretation takes the phrase to mean that he amassed a numerous clan around him.

ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:104:2/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan notes a reading without assimilation and cites a poetic line as evidence: “I am generous to people even when they are miserly.” The poet is unnamed.

ALUSI:104:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī parses alladhī as a full appositive for kull; an unlabelled alternative makes it a partitive appositive.
ALUSI:104:2/r1.anchor: الذي جَمَعَ مَالاً } بدل من { كل } بدل كل

ALUSI:104:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r2.speaker: الجاربردي
ALUSI:104:2/r2.claim: Al-Jarbardī permits alladhī to be an adjective because kull is definite, by analogy with al-Zamakhsharī's analysis of 50:21; al-Ālūsī objects to this.
ALUSI:104:2/r2.anchor: وقال الجاربردي يجوز أن يكون صفة له لأنه معرفة على ما ذكره الزمخشري

ALUSI:104:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r3.claim: The phrase may be accusative or nominative as a form of censure.
ALUSI:104:2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا أو مرفوعا على الذم

ALUSI:104:2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r4.claim: The indefinite mālan magnifies and multiplies the wealth; reports about al-Akhnas say he had four or ten thousand dinars.
ALUSI:104:2/r4.anchor: وتنكير مالا للتفخيم والتكثير وقد كان عند القائلين إنها نزلت في الأخنس أربعة آلاف دينار

ALUSI:104:2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r5.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite form diminishes the wealth as insignificant and contemptible in God's sight.
ALUSI:104:2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للتحقير والتقليل باعتبار أنه عند الله تعالى أقل وأحقر شيء

ALUSI:104:2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r6.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والحمزة والكسائي
ALUSI:104:2/r6.claim: These readers geminate the mīm in jamaʿa for an intensive sense, fitting its coordination with ʿaddadah.
ALUSI:104:2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والاخوان جمع بشد الميم للتكثير

ALUSI:104:2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r7.claim: He repeatedly counted his wealth because of his love and passion for it.

ALUSI:104:2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r8.speaker: التأويلات
ALUSI:104:2/r8.claim: One explanation says he divided the wealth into kinds, such as real estate, goods, and coins.
ALUSI:104:2/r8.anchor: وقيل جعله أصنافا وأنواعا كعقار ومتاع ونقود حكاه في التأويلات

ALUSI:104:2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r9.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI:104:2/r9.claim: Several scholars say he made the wealth a reserve for the calamities and hardships of time.
ALUSI:104:2/r9.anchor: وقال غير واحد أي جعله عدة ومدخرا لنوائب الدهر ومصائبه

ALUSI:104:2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r10.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
ALUSI:104:2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī read ʿaddadahu lightly, without gemination.

ALUSI:104:2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r11.claim: On one reading it is a past verb meaning he counted it, with dissimilation contrary to the usual rule; the cited poetic line supports the unusual form.
ALUSI:104:2/r11.anchor: فهو فعل ماض فك إدغامه على خلاف القياس كما في قوله

ALUSI:104:2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r12.claim: Alternatively it is the noun for a count, coordinated with māl: he collected the wealth and carefully counted it; al-Kashf says this does not require an awkward construction.
ALUSI:104:2/r12.anchor: هو اسم بمعنى العدد المعروف معطوف على ماله أي جمع ماله وضبط عدده وأحصاه

ALUSI:104:2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:104:2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:104:2/r13.claim: A further noun sense is followers and supporters; he collected wealth and a numerous supporting retinue.
ALUSI:104:2/r13.anchor: وقيل هو اسم بمعنى الاتباع والأنصار يقال فلان ذو عدد وعدد

BAGHAWI:104:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:104:2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحفص وحمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI:104:2/r1.claim: These readers geminate the mīm in jamaʿa for an intensive sense; the remaining readers read it lightly.
BAGHAWI:104:2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ،   وابن عامر ،   وحفص ،   وحمزة ،   والكسائي : { جمع } بتشديد الميم على التكثير

BAGHAWI:104:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:104:2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:104:2/r2.claim: ʿAddadahu means he counted and kept account of the wealth.

BAGHAWI:104:2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:104:2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI:104:2/r3.claim: Muqātil says he prepared, stored, and made it a provision for himself; Arabic uses aʿdadtu and ʿadadtuhu for keeping something back.
BAGHAWI:104:2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل : استعده وادخره وجعله عتاداً له

BAYDAWI:104:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:104:2/r1.claim: The relative clause may substitute for كل, or it may be a nominative or accusative expression of blame.
BAYDAWI:104:2/r1.anchor: { الذي جمع مالا } بدل من كل أو ذم منصوب أو مرفوع

BAYDAWI:104:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI:104:2/r2.claim: They read ʿaddadahu with a doubled consonant, signaling repeated counting or accumulation as provisions for calamities.
BAYDAWI:104:2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بالتشديد للتكثير وعدده

BAYDAWI:104:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:104:2/r3.claim: The doubled form can mean counting the wealth again and again.

BAYDAWI:104:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:104:2/r4.speaker: قُرئ
BAYDAWI:104:2/r4.claim: A reading that separates the assimilation supports the doubled reading.
BAYDAWI:104:2/r4.anchor: ويؤيده أنه قرئ ( وعدده ) على فك الإدغام

BIQAI:104:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:2/r1.claim: The wealthy who needlessly hoard are especially blameworthy in a culture that treats accumulation as success and boasts of profit; this description exposes the true loser.
BIQAI:104:2/r1.anchor: ولما كان الذي يفعل النقيصة من غير حاجة تحوجه إليها

BIQAI:104:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
BIQAI:104:2/r2.claim: These readers double the consonant in jamaʿa to signal abundant accumulation; others lighten it because the basic verb already conveys collecting.
BIQAI:104:2/r2.anchor: جاء التشديد في فعله لأبي جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي

BIQAI:104:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:2/r3.claim: The unaugmented form of collecting inherently indicates abundance, unlike counting, which can refer to a small number.

BIQAI:104:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:2/r4.claim: All readers agree on doubling ʿaddada because the undoubled form can refer to counting only a few things.

BIQAI:104:2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:2/r5.claim: The wealth is great, and repeated counting stresses its abundance.

BIQAI:104:2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:104:2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:104:2/r6.claim: He either keeps so much that counting it takes a long time or hoards it as a reserve against worldly troubles.
BIQAI:104:2/r6.anchor: أي جعله بحيث إذا أريد عدده طال الزمان فيه وكثر التعداد

IBNASHUR:104:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r1.claim: This adds greed for wealth to the subject's disgraceful traits; it arises from avarice and fear of poverty and targets those known for mocking and defaming Muslims, reportedly the occasion for the warning.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r1.anchor: وأتبع { الذي جمع مالاً وعدده } لزيادة تشنيع صفتيه الذميمتين بصفة الحرص على المال . وإنما ينشأ ذلك عن بخل النفس والتخوف من الفقر

IBNASHUR:104:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r2.claim: The relative clause is another adjective for the same person; multiple descriptions may appear without conjunction, as in the cited passage in al-Qalam.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r2.anchor: واسم الموصول من قوله : { الذي جمع مالاً } نعت آخر ولم يعطف { الذي } بالواو لأن ذكر الأوصاف المتعددة للموصوف الواحد يجوز أن يكون بدون عطف

IBNASHUR:104:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r3.claim: مال is what a person acquires to meet needs such as food and clothing, including livestock and fruit-bearing trees; what counts most as wealth varies by livelihood.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r3.anchor: والمال : مكاسب الإِنسان التي تنفعه وتكفي مؤونة حاجته من طعام ولباس وما يتخذ منه ذلك كالأنعام والأشجار ذات الثمار المثمرة

IBNASHUR:104:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r4.claim: Among nomadic Arabs, wealth chiefly meant camels; Zuhayr's verse describes camels paid as blood money.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r4.anchor: فغلب اسم المال بين أهل الخيام على الإِبل

IBNASHUR:104:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r5.claim: For settled people with gardens, مال commonly means date palms; Abu Hurayrah and Abu Talhah use the word this way.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r5.anchor: وهو عند أهل القرى الذين يتخذون الحوائط يغلب على النخل يقولون خرج فلان إلى مَاله ، أي إلى جناته

IBNASHUR:104:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR:104:2/r6.claim: Abu Hurayrah says the Ansar were occupied with work in their possessions, using مال for their gardens and palms.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r6.anchor: وفي كلام أبي هريرة :   "  وإن إخواني الأنصار شغلهم العمل في أموالهم

IBNASHUR:104:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r7.speaker: أبو طلحة
IBNASHUR:104:2/r7.claim: Abu Talhah calls the well of Haa his most beloved مال, meaning his garden and property.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو طلحة : « وإن أحب أموالي إليَّ بئرُ حاء

IBNASHUR:104:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r8.claim: Among Meccan traders, مال commonly meant dirhams; the Prophet's question to al-ʿAbbas about wealth held by Umm al-Fadl is an example.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r8.anchor: وغلب عند أهل مكة على الدراهم لأن أهل مكة أهل تجر

IBNASHUR:104:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r9.claim: The word مال was discussed earlier in the command to spend from what one loves.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r9.anchor: وتقدم في قوله تعالى : { لن تنالوا البر حتى تنفقوا مما تحبون } سورة آل عمران

IBNASHUR:104:2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r10.claim: عدده means counting wealth repeatedly; the doubled form intensifies the action and its recurrence.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r10.anchor: ومعنى : { عدده } أكْثر من عدِّه ، أي حسابه لشدة ولعه بجمعه فالتضعيف للمبالغة في ( عدَّ ) ومعاودته

IBNASHUR:104:2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r11.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:104:2/r11.claim: The majority read جمع مالاً with a light mīm.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r11.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { جمع مالاً } بتخفيف الميم

IBNASHUR:104:2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r12.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب وخلف
IBNASHUR:104:2/r12.claim: These readers pronounce جمع with a doubled mīm, intensifying the collection and pairing the form with عدده.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r12.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب وخلفٌ بتشديد الميم مزاوجاً لقوله : { عدده }

IBNASHUR:104:2/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r13.claim: With the majority reading, the intensive counting indirectly implies effort to amass wealth, since repeated counting is done to increase the hoard.
IBNASHUR:104:2/r13.anchor: وعلى قراءة الجمهور دل تضعيف { عدده } على معنى تكلف جمعه بطريق الكناية لأنه لا يكرر عده إلا ليزيد جمعه

IBNASHUR:104:2/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:104:2/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:104:2/r14.claim: Alternatively, عدده means he amassed a range of types, comparable to the listed kinds of worldly goods in another verse.
